items.comment: Accurately describes writer.println(s) appending a line plus separator to the file; @param wording is consistent with the trait's existing out doc.
Accurate, mirrors out's phrasing appropriately for the error stream.

Correctly states f is evaluated with no additional buffering, consistent with trait's note that library implementations run unbuffered. Tags for @tparam/@param/@return are accurate and in house style (lowercase, no trailing period).

"Closes the writer to the file" exposes the private `writer` field, an implementation detail not part of the public API surface. Clearer as something like "Closes the file, flushing any output not yet written." Not a factual error (writer.close() does flush then close), just a style leak.
Same issue as close: references the internal `writer` rather than framing it in terms of the file/stream the API exposes.
